children: Super Heavy booster diverted to an ocean splashdown instead of returning for capture by the launch tower’s mechanical arms during Starship Flight 15, according to the live mission update provided for this report. The reason for the aborted capture wasn't immediately clear.
The diversion ends the mission’s prospect of achieving SpaceX’s

planned first recovery of both rocket stages using tower catches. The company had intended to catch Super Heavy shortly after launch, followed by the Starship upper stage after a much longer orbital mission. The catches were planned as separate events, roughly a day apart.

The Starship upper stage continued toward its planned orbit, according to the same live update. Its mission objectives include deploying 26 next-generation Starlink V3 internet satellites and attempting its first return to the launch site for a tower catch. Orbital insertion, satellite deployment and upper-stage recovery remained unconfirmed at the stage described here.
For investors, the booster diversion leaves a key part of SpaceX’s

intended operating model undemonstrated on this flight: recovering both stages for reuse. Routine recovery and repeated flights would help establish whether Starship can deliver the lower launch costs and higher flight frequency underpinning its commercial ambitions.
Satellite deployment remains a separate milestone. Completing that objective would advance Starship’s role in expanding SpaceX’s
Starlink network, even with the booster catch abandoned.
